bug_semantics: ClassroomIO v0.1.13 exposed its Supabase/PostgREST public.course resource to low-privilege authenticated clients. A student could replace the application's scoped POST with GET /rest/v1/course and supply an arbitrary relational select. The effective course SELECT policy admitted every published course as well as courses whose group contained the caller, while group, groupmember, and profile rows were globally readable. PostgREST followed the course->group->groupmember->profile and course->lesson->profile foreign keys, so the response disclosed course metadata, membership records, other students, and tutor profiles without an authorization decision tied to the requested relation set or HTTP method.
flaw_origin: The first public-history writer is a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab (#19: Implement supabase local setup), which imported the remote schema and in one ordinary commit added the course/group/groupmember/profile tables and foreign keys, GRANT ALL on those tables to anon and authenticated, a course SELECT USING (true) policy, and a profile SELECT USING (true) policy. The commit is a schema import of an already existing remote database, so the production database may have predated the repository representation, but no earlier public commit contains the causal schema. Later RLS work preserved rather than originated the read exposure: 20240717053936_rls.sql enabled RLS yet created SELECT USING (true) policies for group and groupmember, and 20250808030821_rls_secure_courses.sql only narrowed course rows to is_published OR course-group/admin membership.
ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file -p a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab` shows author and committer `Rotimi Best <best@classroomio.com>`, one parent, and only the message `#19: Implement supabase local setup`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI trailer, or other AI marker in the BIC commit object.
evidence: Advisory reproduction and scope: https://github.com/classroomio/classroomio/issues/642 identifies affected v0.1.13 and records a student changing POST to GET /rest/v1/course with a select expanding group(*,members:groupmember(*,profile(*))) and lesson teacher profiles; the returned data includes other student profiles, tutor information, group membership, and internal course metadata. GHSA-rx88-8j23-4qxx/CVE-2025-67259 gives the same mechanism and CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N.

Affected-tag schema: `git grep -n -E 'create policy|CREATE POLICY' v0.1.13 -- supabase/migrations/20231115082347_remote_schema.sql supabase/migrations/20240717053936_rls.sql supabase/migrations/20250808030821_rls_secure_courses.sql` finds the original course `FOR SELECT USING (true)` and profile `FOR SELECT USING (true)` policies, the later group/groupmember/profile read policies, and the final course policy. `git show v0.1.13:supabase/migrations/20250808030821_rls_secure_courses.sql` shows the effective course predicate `using ((is_published OR is_user_in_course_group_or_admin(group_id)))`.

Relational exposure at the first writer: `git grep -n -E 'CREATE TABLE.*(course|group|groupmember|profile|lesson)' a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab -- supabase/migrations/20231115082347_remote_schema.sql` locates all five tables. In the same file, constraints at lines 865, 880, 883, 901, and 910 connect course to group, group to groupmember, groupmember to profile, lesson to course, and lesson teacher_id to profile. Grants at lines 1062-1064, 1078-1080, 1090-1092, 1094-1096, and 1166-1168 grant ALL on those resources to anon/authenticated/service_role. Those foreign keys are what allow PostgREST relational expansion.

Effective v0.1.13 RLS still permits the attack: `git show v0.1.13:supabase/migrations/20240717053936_rls.sql | sed -n '550,720p'` shows group and groupmember `for select to public using (true)`. Its profile section around lines 1075-1081 has `for select to authenticated, anon using (true)`. `git grep -n -E 'alter table "public"."(course|group|groupmember)" enable row level security' v0.1.13 -- supabase/migrations/20240717053936_rls.sql` confirms RLS is enabled, so these permissive predicates, rather than absent enforcement by accident, are the effective authorization rules.

BIC search: `git log --all --reverse -S'GRANT ALL ON TABLE "public"."groupmember" TO "authenticated"' -- '**/*.sql'` first reports a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab. `git log -L 938,954:supabase/migrations/20231115082347_remote_schema.sql v0.1.13` initially stops at 50e89f90c9f264ac93cc6882743e21ed70a9f011 because that commit reverted a temporary migration squash. Repeating `git log -L 938,954:supabase/migrations/20231115082347_remote_schema.sql d010531ef7932dc3093621f1771abb90c0b14368^` bypasses the delete/revert artifact and traces the course/profile permissive policies to a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab. Thus neither d010531ef7932dc3093621f1771abb90c0b14368 nor its revert is treated as an introducer.

Direct parent absence: `git cat-file -p a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab` names sole parent 78732f95f3372f3d2b0a1aca2e9be6af1a98a1cc. `git diff --name-status 78732f95f3372f3d2b0a1aca2e9be6af1a98a1cc a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab -- supabase/migrations/20231115082347_remote_schema.sql` reports `A`; `git ls-tree -r --name-only 78732f95f3372f3d2b0a1aca2e9be6af1a98a1cc -- supabase` contains config/functions/seed only and no schema migration or equivalent course/group grants/policies.

Version boundary: `git tag --contains a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab --sort=version:refname` includes every repository release tag from v0.1.0 through 0.2.11 and later; v0.1.13 resolves to commit 876a785b3c467b809804f56e0981bff448fcfdb5 and contains the vulnerable migrations. The advisory only claims/testing-proves v0.1.13, so the tag-containment result establishes code presence, not independent runtime testing of every tag.

Rejected apparent fix: one-parent landing commit 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052 (`feat: complete rewrite of course (#622)`) removed the Supabase migration tree on main and is first contained by v0.3.0. Its tree 3a25148b9e8ce8f6d36e0b207dd7edbe9f3692e3 exactly equals PR-head f742cb1242b3f0f2012e44c20907863d1229a296, proving it is a squash landing. PR member f5c67b021c7f7496ffa85d76c470df97f9940857 deletes the Supabase files, but this is transport replacement, not a closing access-control fix.

Why no fix SHA is claimed: PR member 35dbde0378bd95b400c1763e49ba8191e1515ee7 added the replacement public unauthenticated GET /course/slug/:slug handler, and `git log --all -S'getCourse(undefined, slug)' -- apps/api/src/routes/course/course.ts` traces it to that member and the 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052 squash. At current HEAD f08f6c6838259ca440299a82f5d100d44d5349cd, apps/api/src/routes/course/course.ts lines 112-125 still label the route public, apply no auth/member middleware, call getCourse(undefined, slug), and serialize the result. packages/db/src/queries/course/course.ts lines 333-475 defines that result as the entire course plus group members, profile id/fullname/username/avatar/email, attendance, contentItems, and organization settings; the slug query checks only slug and status ACTIVE, not isPublished or membership. Therefore the rewrite retires /rest/v1/course but preserves the advisory's root semantic disclosure through a first-party endpoint, and no later public commit/tag is a real closing fix.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab` is the complete commit object used for attribution. AI-related trailers on the much later 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052 rewrite/fix candidate are deliberately ignored under the protocol because they are not evidence on the BIC.
reasoning: The security boundary was always supposed to be enforced by the server-side database/API layer, because a student controls the HTTP method and PostgREST select expression. The initial checked-in Supabase schema made course, group, groupmember, lesson, and profile data directly queryable and relationally expandable. Subsequent RLS migrations did not cure that causal error: course visibility remained public-or-member and the nested membership/profile relations remained globally readable. Git -S and line history, after explicitly bypassing the later squash/revert artifact, converge on a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab; its direct parent lacks the migration and causal rules. The BIC commit object is plainly human-authored and has no AI marker, so NOT_AI is supported independently of later history. No fix SHA is assigned: the March 2026 rewrite removed Supabase/PostgREST but its landed replacement exposes essentially the same sensitive relation graph from an unauthenticated slug route, and that code remains at current main. An endpoint rename/architectural refactor is not a root-cause remediation. This is therefore a closed attribution verdict for an explicitly unpatched vulnerability lifecycle, not an EVIDENCE_GAP about AI provenance.
remaining_gap: Unpatched in public history as of current main f08f6c6838259ca440299a82f5d100d44d5349cd: no commit or release can be named as a true fix because the v0.3.0 rewrite removed the reported /rest/v1/course transport while retaining unauthenticated disclosure of course, group-member/profile email, attendance, content, and organization data at GET /course/slug/:slug. Deployment-specific confirmation of which commit was running when issue #642 was closed is not public, but that does not supply a source-level closing fix.
